sense: what you hold over you in the rain

pins.definition: A folding object with a cloth cover that you hold over your head to stay dry in the rain.
A folding object that you hold over your head to stay dry when it is raining.
A folding fabric canopy on a handle, carried for protection against rain or sun.

situation: A lone woman walks along a rain-slicked stone path during a heavy downpour.
subject: the umbrella
brief: A woman holds an open, dark oiled-paper umbrella high against a torrential slate-gray rainstorm, the taut canopy taking the full force of the driving vertical streaks while keeping her head and shoulders entirely dry.
prompt: A woman holds an open, dark oiled-paper umbrella high against a torrential slate-gray rainstorm, the taut canopy taking the full force of the driving vertical streaks while keeping her head and shoulders entirely dry. a Japanese ukiyo-e woodblock print, flat layered colour planes, Prussian blue and vermilion, visible woodgrain and registration edges, weather and motion stylised into pattern. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
